claims.text: USAspending records approximately $135 billion in prime contract obligations to Leidos-named recipient entities since FY2008.

The UAP Records Collection established by NDAA FY2024 Sec. 1841 consists of record copies of all 'Government, Government-provided, or Government-funded records' relating to UAP, technologies of unknown origin and non-human intelligence.

desc: Leidos is what SAIC's government services business became in the 2013 split, and it is now among the largest holders of classified IT, intelligence analysis and technical services work in the federal government - USAspending records roughly $135 billion in prime contract obligations to Leidos entities since FY2008, with the recipient list running to the hundred-record query limit. In 2020 it acquired Dynetics, the Huntsville engineering house whose own federal prime obligations exceed $4 billion. Leidos matters to this domain for a reason that has nothing to do with allegations of material: it is the corporate layer through which classified data, records and analytical products physically pass. If a UAP records collection exists inside DoD or the intelligence community, the systems holding it, the personnel indexing it and the security architecture protecting it are in substantial part contracted out to firms of this type. The NDAA FY2024 records provisions require transmission of 'Government, Government-provided, or Government-funded records' to the National Archives - a formulation that reaches contractor-held records - and no public accounting has been made of what any services prime holds.
